title: Adoption reality report and capability truth boundary
rawUserRequest: Deliver WI-13 as an adoption reality report that separates template capability truth from adopter-repository verified state across installation, calibration, hosted CI, branch protection and external identity, CodeQL, SBOM, provenance, signing, and production sandbox. Unknown, not-configured, and external-responsibility states must remain explicit. Keep Outcome/task_report machine-readable and human-readable without overclaiming.

declaredIntent.summary: Expose a deterministic adoption report that makes template capability and adopter evidence visibly separate.

outOfScope: Changing WI-11 governance configuration depth or WI-12 performance diagnosis.
Authenticating provider accounts, inspecting hosted provider state, or proving adopter execution from this template checkout.
Implementing CodeQL, SBOM, provenance, signing, sandbox, branch protection, or identity providers.
Changing Capability Truth Matrix statuses or immutable archived Work Item evidence.
Changing Outcome derivation or task_report projection rules; this Work Item only documents and tests their delivery boundary.

sources.reason: Defines Repository Truth, Delegated Domain Evidence, Capability Truth, and external boundaries.
Canonical distinction between implemented, template_only, adopter_installed, and planned.
Machine-readable template capability rows and limitations.
Adopter-owned control inventory and not_verified boundary.
Existing fail-closed adopter evidence conventions and template-owned evidence exclusion.
Canonical Outcome/task_report projection and status delivery path.

riskAssessment.reason: A report that conflates template files with adopter or provider evidence could create unsafe readiness claims; missing external facts must remain explicit.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: The report is a bounded repository-local evidence presentation and does not perform external operations.

preReviewWarnings: Repository-local files must never be presented as adopter or provider verification.
Unknown, not_configured, not_verified, and external_responsibility states must remain machine-visible and human-readable.
Outcome/task_report remain derived projections; do not create a second authoritative result.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A deterministic machine-readable adoption reality report separates template capability rows from adopter state and never promotes template_only evidence to adopter_installed.

The report covers installation, calibration, hosted CI, branch protection, external identity, CodeQL, SBOM, provenance, signing, and production sandbox with explicit verified, not_configured, unknown, and external_responsibility semantics.
The report fails closed for malformed state, unsupported status, template-owned release evidence presented as adopter evidence, and claims that lack an evidence reference.
Human-readable documentation explains the same states and boundaries, including that production sandbox and provider controls remain adopter responsibility.
Focused TDD tests prove complete, empty, malformed, deterministic, and anti-overclaim cases; Outcome/task_report remain machine-readable and human-readable through existing projections.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Template capability exists but no adopter evidence is supplied.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Template state is reported separately and adopter state is not_configured or external_responsibility; no readiness claim is emitted.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused report tests and documentation review.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Adopter supplies an exact evidence reference for a configured control.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The corresponding control is verified only when its evidence reference is valid and non-template-owned.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Unknown, unsupported, expired, or provider-owned state is supplied.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The report preserves unknown or external_responsibility and never infers completion.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Outcome/task_report projections are inspected after a governed run.
scenarioCoverage.expected: JSON remains machine-readable and Markdown remains human-readable with the same conservative status semantics.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Existing projection tests plus report documentation cross-check.

guidelines: Capability Truth Matrix is authoritative for template capability claims; this report cannot upgrade a matrix status.
Adopter and provider evidence must be referenced explicitly and template-owned release artifacts cannot satisfy adopter verification.
Unknown, not_configured, not_verified, and external_responsibility are distinct states and must not be collapsed.
Outcome/task_report are derived projections; preserve the existing machine-readable JSON and human-readable Markdown pair.
Do not perform network, provider, production, sandbox, identity, signing, or secret operations.

intent.problem: Adoption discussions can mistake template capability files and local checks for evidence that an adopter configured controls or that a provider enforced them. The resulting status is difficult to read and can overstate readiness.
constraints: Keep template truth, adopter evidence, and provider responsibility separate.
Keep the report deterministic and evidence-referenced.
Do not change runtime control implementations or external systems.
Keep Outcome/task_report as the existing derived delivery pair.
intent.rationale: A conservative adoption report gives humans one place to see what the template provides, what the adopter has actually verified, and which controls remain external without turning absence into a false pass.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.
